title: 30 Minute VWAP Expiry Settlement and What It Means for Options Traders
summary: Understand the SEBI panel’s 30-minute VWAP settlement proposal, what it means for options traders, and how to review expiry strategies with AlgoTest.
body_markdown:
As reported on October 15, 2026, SEBI’s Secondary Market Advisory Committee (SMAC) favours using the 3:00 PM to 3:30 PM volume-weighted average price (VWAP) approach for derivatives expiry settlement for at least a year. This would postpone an immediate move to a blended Closing Auction Session (CAS) formula. A final implementing circular and effective date were not verified in this review.


**What should options traders do now?** Review exit rules, test payoffs near the strikes and compare expiry-day results using AlgoTest’s backtesting and simulator tools. Check official implementation details before changing live settlement assumptions or trading hours.


## What is 30 minute VWAP expiry settlement


VWAP means volume-weighted average price. For a stock, it weights eligible transaction prices by the quantity traded during a defined window. Trades with larger quantities have more influence on the average. It is different from the last traded price and from the full-day VWAP indicator on a chart.


SEBI confirmed that CAS, introduced on August 3, 2026, made auction-derived closing prices a basis for derivatives expiry settlement. The review concerns that relationship.[See SEBI’s review statement.](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/sep-2026/1788448619635.pdf)


## Does the VWAP proposal mean CAS is cancelled?


No. Using continuous-session prices for derivatives expiry settlement would exclude auction trades from that benchmark. It would not, by itself, abolish the closing auction for cash-market stocks.


An index is a calculated value, so traders should use the exchange’s applicable settlement methodology. The VWAP of a Nifty futures chart or an option’s premium is not a substitute for the official underlying settlement value.


The reported timing proposal would allow continuous trading in CAS stocks until 3:30 PM, a one-minute transition, CAS from 3:31 PM to 3:40 PM and derivatives trading until 3:45 PM. These are proposed timings. Your broker’s square-off deadline can also be earlier than the exchange close.


## How does the settlement price affect option profit or loss


For an index option held through expiry, the official underlying settlement value determines its intrinsic value. For a call, intrinsic value is the amount by which settlement exceeds the strike, or zero if it does not. The buyer’s net result also accounts for the premium paid and costs.


Consider a hypothetical index call with a strike of 23,000, bought for a premium of 40 points and held through expiry. Compare two possible official settlement values:


**Final settlement value**


**Call intrinsic value**


**Buyer P&L per unit**


22,980


0 points


−40 points


23,060


60 points


+20 points


This illustration excludes charges and taxes. Multiply the per-unit P&L by the contract quantity to calculate the position result. It does not predict the size or direction of any difference between settlement methods.


If the buyer instead sells the option before expiry, the realised result comes from that execution price minus the entry premium. The final settlement calculation no longer determines the closed position’s payoff, although settlement expectations can influence option prices before the exit.


That distinction is useful when reviewing a strategy: an intraday exit rule and a hold-to-expiry rule answer different questions. Do not evaluate one using the assumptions of the other.


## How could VWAP settlement affect expiry strategies


If implemented, a continuous-session VWAP benchmark would change the price reference used for expiry outcomes. Traders should reassess exit timing, strike exposure and any entry rule built around CAS. It would not establish that a short straddle, strangle or spread is more profitable. The following comparisons are ideas to test.


**Strategy**


**What to examine**


**A useful comparison**


Short straddle


Losses when the underlying moves away from the shared strike


Keep entries fixed; compare earlier exits with your existing exit


Short strangle


The threatened short leg and the effect of adjustments


Compare the same strike-selection rule with and without a predefined adjustment


Same-expiry vertical spread


Net payoff across both strikes and execution of both legs


Compare the whole spread, including hedge cost and charges


Late-session directional trade


Whether the entry depends on an auction move or continuous-market signal


Review results separately for each market structure


For a short straddle, the collected premium provides a limited cushion against an adverse move. A short strangle uses different strikes but still carries substantial directional risk. A VWAP-based benchmark would not remove that exposure.


For a vertical spread, the textbook expiry payoff assumes the intended legs, quantities and expiry remain intact. Closing a protective leg early changes the position. A spread also needs to be assessed after execution costs, not only from its payoff diagram.


If a late-session setup was designed around CAS behaviour, write down exactly what triggers it. An auction-driven price movement, a futures breakout and a time-based premium sale are different entry rules. Keeping the same clock time after a market-structure change does not establish that the original trade logic still holds.

## What should options traders check before changing a strategy


### 1. Separate a VWAP signal from settlement VWAP.


A strategy that buys above an intraday VWAP indicator is using a trading signal. The reported rule concerns an expiry benchmark. Do not assume a chart crossover predicts where the exchange will settle the contract.


### 2. Review the exit before changing the entry.


Write down whether you intend to exit intraday or carry through settlement. Check the instrument, product type, broker square-off deadline and automation settings together. Extending an exit because longer market hours are proposed would change the trade’s exposure.


### 3. Test positions near your strikes.


Evaluate several hypothetical final values around the short strike, breakeven and hedge strike. Use the whole position’s payoff. A small remaining premium is not, by itself, evidence that a short option has little risk.


### 4. Separate historical periods.


Review pre-CAS results and results from August 3, 2026 onward separately. If revised rules are implemented, collect a third sample from the actual effective date. Differences may also reflect volatility or trend, so a before-and-after comparison cannot isolate the effect of regulation on its own.


### 5. Keep position size consistent during testing.


Changing quantity, stops and entry time together makes it harder to identify why results changed. Compare one rule at a time, include costs and examine the worst outcomes. Do not increase size simply because the news sounds favourable to option sellers.

## How to review an expiry strategy on AlgoTest


Use[AlgoTest backtesting](https://algotest.in/feature/backtest) to compare rules across historical sessions, then use the simulator to examine how individual trades developed. The workflow below is a proposed test plan; it does not present backtested results.


**Start with your existing strategy.** Keep the underlying, strike-selection method, entry rule, stop-loss, re-entry settings and quantity unchanged. Save its results as your baseline.


**Filter for expiry days.** Use[AlgoTest’s DTE filter](https://docs.algotest.in/Time-Based-Algo-Trading/backtest-filters/dte-filter/) with DTE = 0 to focus on expiry-day observations. This avoids mixing the behaviour you are studying with non-expiry sessions.


**Compare a small set of exits.** For example, test exits at 2:45 PM, 3:00 PM and 3:15 PM where supported by the selected data and strategy. These are comparison points, not recommended exit times. Hold other settings fixed and use the same dates for each run.


**Compare risk as well as profit.** Record net results after costs, maximum drawdown, the largest losing trade and the number of observations. Look at individual expiry days: one exceptional session can make an otherwise weak variant appear attractive. Check the candidate rule on a separate date range before relying on it.


AlgoTest’s[backtest-results guide](https://docs.algotest.in/Time-Based-Algo-Trading/Backtest-Analysis-and-Pricing/backtesting-results/) explains the available performance metrics and slippage. An earlier exit may reduce exposure to the final part of the session, but it can also give up profitable trades; the comparison should show that trade-off.


**Replay difficult sessions.** In the[AlgoTest simulator](https://docs.algotest.in/clicktrade/simulator/analysis-adjustment/) , inspect the position’s MTM, payoff and Greeks through selected historical sessions. Compare keeping the position intact with a predefined exit or adjustment. Custom entry and exit prices can help examine sensitivity to fills; record those assumptions explicitly.


Choose replay dates before looking at the outcome, and advance through them without using later prices to decide earlier actions. A successful adjustment chosen after seeing the full day is not evidence that the same decision could have been made live.


Historical option data reflects the conditions that actually existed. Replaying a CAS-era session does not recreate how that session would have unfolded under a different settlement regime. Confirm data coverage and expiry handling before treating a test as evidence about final settlement.


If your strategy specifically uses auction information, keep the[AlgoTest CAS Trading Terminal guide](https://algotest.in/blog/where-to-track-indicative-closing-price-live-during-cas/) alongside this review. Use indicative prices to study the auction, and distinguish them from executable option prices and the final official settlement value.


## Conclusion


The practical response to the VWAP proposal is to review your expiry assumptions. Define how you exit, examine the payoff near your strikes and test whether a rule change improves results across multiple sessions. **FAQs**


**Q: Does 30-minute VWAP settlement make option selling safer?**


A: It would change how the settlement benchmark is calculated if implemented. It does not remove directional losses, execution risk or the risks of holding short options near expiry.


**Q: Should I exit all options before 3 PM?**


A: There is no universal exit time established by this news. Compare exit rules for your strategy and check your broker’s deadlines. An earlier exit can change both the risk and the return.


**Q: Can I backtest the proposed settlement rule on AlgoTest?**


A: You can study supported historical strategies and compare exit rules. That does not automatically reproduce a proposed settlement regime. Confirm the platform’s data and settlement handling before testing a position held through expiry.
